topics.name: Types and components of computer systems

questions.q: Which is an example of system software?
questions.why: System software runs the computer; application software does user tasks.

questions.q: RAM is best described as
o: volatile memory that holds data in use
questions.why: Its contents are lost when power is off.

questions.q: Which type of memory holds the start-up instructions and is not lost when power is off?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): some candidates gave RAM rather than ROM; RAM is volatile.

questions.q: What is a major advantage of a Graphical User Interface (GUI) over a Command Line Interface (CLI)?
o: It uses significantly less RAM and CPU processing power
It executes batch operations faster for advanced administrators
It is intuitive and accessible with icons and pointers without memorising commands
It does not require a visual monitor
questions.why: GUIs use WIMP (windows, icons, menus, pointer) metaphors that allow everyday users to interact visually without typing command syntax.

questions.q: Which technology overlays computer-generated images onto a live view of the real world, for example through a phone camera?
questions.why: Augmented reality adds digital content on top of the real view; virtual reality replaces the real world with a fully computer-generated one.

long.q: Describe the differences between RAM and ROM, and give one use of each.
scheme: B1: RAM is volatile: its contents are lost when the power is off
B1: RAM holds the programs and data currently in use, and can be read and written
B1: ROM is non-volatile and read-only: contents are kept without power
B1: ROM holds the start-up (boot) instructions

long.q: Compare a Graphical User Interface (GUI) with a Command Line Interface (CLI), and explain why network administrators often prefer a CLI.
scheme: B1: GUI uses visual elements (windows, icons, menus, pointer - WIMP), making it accessible for non-technical users
B1: CLI requires users to type specific syntax commands from memory, demanding higher technical training
B1: CLI requires far less RAM and processor overhead, allowing it to run over low-bandwidth remote connections
B1: CLI supports powerful scripting and batch execution of administrative tasks across hundreds of remote servers

questions.q: Which is a direct data entry device?
questions.why: It captures data without typing.

questions.q: A sensor in a greenhouse is an
questions.why: It sends readings to the computer.

questions.q: Which is an input device?
questions.why: Actuators and speakers are output devices.

questions.q: Which input technology is used to read bank cheques quickly and reliably even if written over?
questions.why: Cheques use magnetic ink with iron oxide; MICR readers sense magnetic fields so signatures or dirt across the line do not hinder reading.

questions.q: A school wants to mark multiple-choice answer sheets automatically, where students shade a box for each answer. Which input method is most suitable?
questions.why: OMR detects the position of shaded marks on a form, which is exactly what an answer sheet needs; OCR reads printed characters and MICR reads magnetic ink.

long.q: A supermarket uses barcode readers at its checkouts. Give two advantages of barcode readers over typing in product codes, and one disadvantage.
scheme: B1: faster data entry, so shorter queues
B1: more accurate: avoids typing errors
B1: a disadvantage, e.g. damaged or dirty barcodes won't scan and must be typed; cost of the equipment

questions.q: Which has no moving parts?
questions.why: SSDs use flash memory.

questions.q: Magnetic tape is best for
questions.why: Serial access suits archives.

questions.q: Why is a solid-state drive faster than a hard disk drive?
o: It has no moving parts, so data is accessed electronically
questions.why: SSDs also use less power and are more robust.

questions.q: Why are Solid State Drives (SSDs) preferred over magnetic hard disk drives (HDDs) in laptops?
o: They have infinite read-write rewrite cycles
They cost less per gigabyte than optical discs
They have no moving parts, lower latency, and higher shock resistance
questions.why: SSDs use flash memory with zero mechanical latency, consume less power, and withstand physical drops far better than spinning HDDs.

questions.q: Which type of storage reads data by shining a laser at the surface and detecting pits and lands?
questions.why: Optical media such as DVDs and Blu-ray discs are read by a laser; magnetic storage uses read/write heads and solid-state storage has no moving parts.

long.q: Give three reasons why a laptop is more likely to have a solid-state drive (SSD) than a hard disk drive (HDD).
scheme: B1: no moving parts, so it's less likely to be damaged if dropped
B1: faster access to data, so quicker start-up and loading
B1: lighter, smaller or uses less power, so longer battery life

topics.name: Networks and the effects of using them

questions.q: What does a router do?
o: connects a local network to other networks such as the internet
questions.why: It forwards packets between networks.

questions.q: Which is a benefit of cloud storage?
o: files can be accessed from anywhere with internet
questions.why: Access anywhere; relies on connection and the provider.

questions.q: What does a router do on a home network?
o: Connects the home network to the internet and forwards packets
questions.why: Many routers include a wireless access point.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a Local Area Network (LAN) and a Wide Area Network (WAN)?
o: A LAN always uses satellite links while a WAN uses copper cables
A LAN covers a small geographic site while a WAN spans multiple distant geographic locations
A LAN cannot connect to the internet
A WAN is owned and managed by a single private individual
questions.why: LANs are confined to a single building, campus, or home; WANs (like the internet or multinational corporate nets) connect geographically dispersed sites.

questions.q: Which network device sends data only to the device it is meant for, using that device's MAC address?
questions.why: A switch checks the destination MAC address and forwards data only to that device; a hub broadcasts to every device, and a router uses IP addresses to pass data between networks.

long.q: Describe two advantages and two disadvantages of storing files in the cloud rather than on a computer's own hard drive.
scheme: B1: advantage, e.g. files can be reached from any device with an internet connection
B1: a second advantage, e.g. the provider backs up the data; easy to share and work together
B1: disadvantage, e.g. needs a reliable internet connection
B1: a second disadvantage, e.g. security depends on a third party; ongoing subscription cost

long.q: Explain how a proxy server operates to provide security and caching on an educational institution's network.
scheme: B1: the proxy server acts as an intermediary between local client computers and external internet web servers
B1: clients send web requests to the proxy, which hides the client's internal private IP address from the outside world
B1: proxy server caches frequently visited web pages on local storage, reducing external WAN bandwidth consumption
B1: proxy server checks requested URLs against blacklists and content filters, blocking prohibited material

questions.q: Repetitive strain injury can be reduced by
questions.why: A health issue, not a safety one.

questions.q: Which is a health risk from using a computer for a long time?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): safety and health refer to the user, not damage to the equipment.

questions.q: Which is an effect of microprocessor-controlled devices in the home?
o: More leisure time because chores are automated
questions.why: Consider both positive and negative effects.

questions.q: Which health problem is most reduced by using an adjustable chair and sitting with a straight back?
o: Repetitive strain injury in the fingers
questions.why: Poor posture causes back and neck ache, which an adjustable chair helps prevent; eye strain and glare headaches are reduced by breaks and anti-glare screens.

questions.q: Which is a negative effect of using microprocessor-controlled devices in the home?
o: Heating can be switched on remotely before arriving home
The washing machine can run while the owner is out
People may become lazy and less active as they rely on the devices
Food can be cooked with less supervision
questions.why: Relying on devices to do jobs can lead to a less active, unhealthy lifestyle; the other options are benefits.

long.q: Describe two health problems caused by using a computer for long periods, and one way of reducing each.
scheme: B1: a problem, e.g. repetitive strain injury (RSI) from typing or using a mouse
B1: matching remedy, e.g. ergonomic keyboard or mouse, wrist rest, regular breaks
B1: a second problem, e.g. eye strain and headaches; back or neck pain
B1: matching remedy, e.g. anti-glare screen and breaks; adjustable chair and correct posture

questions.q: An expert system includes a knowledge base and
questions.why: Plus a rules base and user interface.

questions.q: Which is an example of a computer-controlled system?
questions.why: Sensors feed readings to a microprocessor that controls outputs.

questions.q: Which is a use of a computer in a school?
o: Recording attendance with a management system
questions.why: Others: timetables, learning platforms, reports.

questions.q: In an online concert booking system, why is a seat temporarily locked once a customer selects it?
o: To stop the same seat being sold to two customers
To make the website load faster
To encrypt the customer's card details
questions.why: Locking the seat while the booking is completed prevents double booking; the seat is released if the customer does not finish paying.

questions.q: A delivery van's computer works out its exact position from signals sent by several satellites. Which system is this?
questions.why: A GPS receiver calculates its position from the time signals take to arrive from at least three satellites; a GIS displays and analyses data on maps.

long.q: A greenhouse uses a computer-controlled system to keep the temperature between 20 °C and 25 °C. Describe how the system works.
scheme: B1: a temperature sensor measures the temperature
B1: an ADC converts the analogue signal to digital
B1: the microprocessor compares the reading with the preset values (20–25 °C)
B1: below 20 °C it switches the heater on; above 25 °C it opens windows or switches on a fan (using actuators)
B1: the process repeats continuously

questions.q: The correct order is
o: analysis, design, development and testing, implementation, documentation, evaluation
questions.why: Analyse first, evaluate last.

questions.q: Parallel running means
o: the old and new systems run together for a time
the new system replaces the old at once
the system is changed in stages
questions.why: Safer but more costly.

questions.q: Test data for a field 'Age' that accepts 11 to 18. Which is extreme data?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates gave explanations instead of test data. Extreme data is on the boundary of what is accepted.

questions.q: Which system implementation strategy runs the new system and old system simultaneously until the new one proves reliable?
questions.why: Parallel running provides a safety net: if the new system fails, the old system continues operation with zero data loss, despite higher running costs.

questions.q: An analyst needs the views of 400 staff in different branches quickly. Which method of researching the current system is most suitable?
questions.why: Questionnaires can be sent to many people at once and answered quickly and anonymously; interviewing or observing 400 people would take far too long.

long.q: Describe two methods of implementing a new system and give one advantage of each.
scheme: B1: direct changeover: the old system is replaced at once
B1: advantage: fast and cheap, benefits immediately
B1: parallel running: both systems run together
B1: advantage: if the new system fails, the old one is still there

long.q: A hospital is switching to a new electronic patient records system. Evaluate direct changeover versus parallel running.
scheme: B1: direct changeover stops the old system overnight and starts the new system immediately: fast and avoids duplicate data entry
B1: high risk with direct changeover: if the new system has critical bugs, patient care could be disrupted with no fallback
B1: parallel running runs both systems side by side until the new one is proven, so there is a fallback if it fails
B1: disadvantage of parallel running: hospital staff must duplicate all entries in both systems, doubling workload and costs

questions.q: Phishing is
o: fake emails trying to trick you into giving personal details
questions.why: Check sender and links.

questions.q: Encryption
o: makes data unreadable without the key
questions.why: It protects data if intercepted.

questions.q: What is a physical safety risk when using computers?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): many thought 'safety' meant damage to the equipment rather than harm to the user.

questions.q: What encryption mechanism uses a public key to encrypt data and a private key to decrypt it?
questions.why: Asymmetric cryptography uses mathematically linked key pairs: anyone can encrypt using the public key, but only the recipient's private key can decrypt.

questions.q: A user types the correct web address but is secretly taken to a fake copy of the website. What is this called?
questions.why: Pharming uses malicious code or a corrupted DNS entry to redirect a correctly typed address to a fake site; phishing relies on the user clicking a link in a fake email.

long.q: Explain two ways a student could protect their personal data online.
scheme: B1: one method, e.g. strong passwords / two-factor authentication
B1: explained: makes unauthorised access harder
B1: a second method, e.g. not opening links in unexpected emails (phishing) / privacy settings
B1: explained

long.q: Explain how two-factor authentication (2FA) significantly improves security when accessing online financial accounts.
scheme: B1: 2FA requires two distinct authentication factors: something you know (password/PIN) and something you have (phone/token) or are (biometric)
B1: if a cybercriminal steals or guesses the password via phishing or data breaches, they cannot gain access without the second factor
B1: the second factor usually generates a time-sensitive, one-time passcode (OTP) that expires rapidly
B1: an unexpected code request warns the genuine owner that someone else has their password

questions.q: When designing for young children, you should use
o: large text, simple language and images
questions.why: Match the product to its audience.

questions.q: A website is for young children. Which design choice suits the audience?
o: Large text, simple words and bright images
questions.why: Always consider the audience's age and needs.

questions.q: Why find out the audience's needs before designing?
o: So the content, language and design suit them
questions.why: Consider age, experience and accessibility.

questions.q: A presentation is for busy company directors. Which design best suits this audience?
o: Short bullet points with key figures and clear charts
Cartoon images and very simple vocabulary
questions.why: Directors have little time and need the key facts quickly, so concise points and charts suit them; cartoons and heavy animation look unprofessional.

questions.q: Which method helps protect software from being illegally copied and installed?
o: Running a spell check on the program
Saving the files in PDF format
Requiring a unique product key to activate it
questions.why: The software will not install or run without a valid product key or activation code, so an illegal copy is useless; the other options do not restrict use.

long.q: A website is being designed to teach six-year-olds about animals. Describe three ways the design should suit this audience.
scheme: B1: simple language and short sentences
B1: large, clear font with bright colours and plenty of images
B1: simple navigation, e.g. large buttons or icons; sound or animation to keep interest

questions.q: CC in an email means
o: a copy is sent to another recipient visibly
questions.why: BCC hides recipients.

questions.q: What is the generic name for meeting online with sound and video in real time?
questions.why: Examiners (2023): candidates knew trade names for these meetings but not the generic term.

questions.q: Which is a feature of email that saves time when writing to the same group again?
questions.why: Bcc hides the other recipients' addresses.

questions.q: A teacher emails 30 parents and must not let any parent see the others' email addresses. Where should the parents' addresses be entered?
questions.why: Addresses in BCC receive the email but are hidden from all other recipients; addresses in To and CC are visible to everyone.

questions.q: Which is good netiquette when writing an email?
o: Writing the whole message in capital letters so it stands out
Forwarding chain emails to all your contacts
Including other people's personal details without asking
Avoiding capital letters for whole sentences, as they look like shouting
questions.why: Text in capitals is read as shouting, so it is avoided; forwarding chain emails and sharing other people's details are poor netiquette.

long.q: Explain the difference between CC and BCC when sending an email, and describe a situation where BCC should be used.
scheme: B1: CC sends a copy, and every recipient can see who else received it
B1: BCC sends a copy, but the BCC addresses are hidden from other recipients
B1: e.g. sending a newsletter to many customers so their email addresses stay private

questions.q: Which file type is best for a photograph on a web page?
questions.why: JPEG compresses photos well.

questions.q: A CSV file stores
o: data as plain text separated by commas
questions.why: Easy to import into spreadsheets and databases.

questions.q: Which file type is best for a photo on a web page?
questions.why: JPEG uses lossy compression to keep photos small.

questions.q: A document must look exactly the same on any computer and should not be easy to edit. Which file type is best?
questions.why: A PDF keeps the layout, fonts and images fixed on any device and is hard to edit; .rtf and .txt are editable text formats.

questions.q: Which statement about lossy compression is correct?
o: Some data is permanently removed to reduce the file size
The original file can be restored exactly
It always makes the file larger
It is used only for text files
questions.why: Lossy compression (as in JPEG and MP3) deletes detail the user is unlikely to notice, so the original cannot be recovered; lossless compression keeps all the data.

long.q: Explain why a large photograph should be compressed before it is placed on a web page, and name a suitable file type.
scheme: B1: a smaller file size means the page loads faster
B1: it uses less bandwidth and storage
B1: a suitable type, e.g. .jpg

questions.q: To resize an image without distorting it, you should
questions.why: Maintain the proportions.

questions.q: An image is resized without distortion. What has been kept?
questions.why: Lock the aspect ratio before resizing.

questions.q: What does cropping an image do?
o: Removes unwanted outer parts of it
questions.why: Resizing changes its dimensions.

questions.q: An image 800 × 600 pixels is resized with its aspect ratio locked so that its width becomes 400 pixels. What is its new height?
questions.why: Keeping the aspect ratio scales both dimensions by the same factor; the width is halved, so the height becomes 600 ÷ 2 = 300.

questions.q: An image of a car facing left must face right, like a mirror image, without turning upside down. Which tool should be used?
questions.why: Flipping horizontally mirrors the image left to right; rotating by 180° would also turn the car upside down.

long.q: Describe how to make an image half its width in a document without distorting it, and explain how cropping is different from resizing.
scheme: B1: keep (lock) the aspect ratio
B1: e.g. set the width to 50% or drag a corner handle, so the height changes in proportion
B1: cropping removes part of the image; resizing keeps the whole image but changes its size

questions.q: A header in a document
o: appears at the top of every page
questions.why: Footers appear at the bottom.

questions.q: What is a widow in document layout?
o: The last line of a paragraph left alone at the top of a page
questions.why: An orphan is the first line left at the bottom of a page.

questions.q: What are margins in a document?
o: The blank space between the text and the edge of the page
questions.why: Gutter margins allow for binding.

questions.q: Which alignment makes both the left and right edges of a paragraph straight?
questions.why: Fully justified text adds space between words so that each line runs from the left margin to the right margin.

questions.q: A newsletter needs text that flows down one column and then continues at the top of the next, side by side on the page. Which feature should be used?
questions.why: Newspaper-style columns let text flow from the bottom of one column to the top of the next; tab stops only line up text along a single line.

long.q: Explain the difference between a widow and an orphan in a document, and how either can be removed.
scheme: B1: widow: the last line of a paragraph on its own at the top of a new page or column
B1: orphan: the first line of a paragraph on its own at the bottom of a page or column
B1: remove with a page or column break, or by turning on widow/orphan control

questions.q: Using styles in a document helps
questions.why: Change a style once and it updates everywhere.

questions.q: Why use a corporate house style?
o: Documents look consistent and the organisation is recognised
questions.why: It sets fonts, colours, logos and layout.

questions.q: Why use styles in a long document?
o: To apply consistent formatting quickly and build a contents page
questions.why: Change a style once and every heading updates.

questions.q: A house style says body text must use a serif font. Which font meets this rule?
questions.why: Times New Roman has small strokes (serifs) at the ends of its letters; Arial, Verdana and Calibri are sans-serif fonts.

questions.q: The Heading 1 style in a long report is changed to Arial 16 point bold. What happens to the headings that already use Heading 1?
o: All of them update automatically to the new format
Only headings typed after the change are updated
Each heading must be reformatted by hand
Only the first heading on each page changes
questions.why: Text that uses a style takes its formatting from that style, so changing the style updates every heading using it at once.

long.q: A company wants all its documents to follow a corporate house style. Explain two benefits of this and give two things the house style would specify.
scheme: B1: consistency: every document looks the same, so the company is recognisable
B1: saves time: staff don't have to choose formatting each time
B1: an item, e.g. font type and size for headings and body text
B1: a second item, e.g. logo position, colour scheme, margins, line spacing

questions.q: Validation checks that data is
questions.why: Verification checks it was entered accurately.

questions.q: A range check would stop
o: a typo in a postcode that is still valid
questions.why: It checks a value lies between limits.

questions.q: Which validation check makes sure a date of birth is not in the future?
questions.why: Verification (proof-reading, double entry) checks the data was copied correctly.

questions.q: The sentence 'Meat me at the station' passes a spell check without any error being shown. Why?
o: The spell checker is switched off
'Meat' is a correctly spelt word, even though it is the wrong word here
Spell checkers only check proper nouns
The sentence is too short to be checked
questions.why: A spell checker only checks that each word is in its dictionary, so a real word used in the wrong place is missed; this is why proofreading is still needed.

questions.q: Data is typed in twice by different people and the computer compares the two versions. What is this?
questions.why: Double data entry is a verification method: any difference between the two entries shows a copying error. Range and format checks are validation.

long.q: Explain the difference between validation and verification, with an example of each.
scheme: B1: validation: the computer checks data is reasonable / follows rules
B1: e.g. a range check on age
B1: verification: checks data has been entered or copied accurately
B1: e.g. double entry of a password / visual check

questions.q: Which chart best shows parts of a whole?
questions.why: Each sector is a share of the total.

questions.q: What should every chart include?
o: A title and labelled axes or a legend
questions.why: Choose the chart type that fits the data.

questions.q: Which chart shows change over time?
questions.why: Pie charts show parts of a whole.

questions.q: A scientist wants to see whether there is a relationship between hours of revision and exam score for 50 students. Which chart is best?
questions.why: A scatter graph plots one variable against the other for each student, so any correlation shows up as a pattern in the points.

questions.q: A chart must show monthly rainfall in mm and average temperature in °C for the same months. What is the best way to show both clearly?
o: Plot one data series on a secondary vertical axis
Use a pie chart for both
questions.why: The two series have different units and ranges, so a secondary axis gives each its own correctly labelled scale.

long.q: A teacher wants to compare the average test scores of four classes. Which type of chart should be used, and what labels must it have? Describe a situation where a pie chart would be better.
scheme: B1: a bar (column) chart, to compare values across categories
B1: a chart title
B1: axis titles and category labels, e.g. 'Class' and 'Average score (%)'
B1: a pie chart shows parts of a whole, e.g. the proportion of students at each grade

questions.q: Mail merge combines
o: a master document with a data source
questions.why: To personalise letters for many people.

questions.q: What does a page break do?
o: Starts the following text on a new page
questions.why: A section break can also change layout from that point.

questions.q: What is a header?
o: Text that appears at the top of every page
questions.why: Footers appear at the bottom; both often hold page numbers.

questions.q: A report has portrait pages, but one wide table must be on a landscape page. What should be inserted before and after the table?
questions.why: Page orientation can only change between sections, so section breaks are needed; a page break starts a new page but keeps the same orientation.

questions.q: In a mail merge letter, what happens to the merge field «FirstName» when the merge is run?
o: It is replaced by each customer's first name from the data source
The word FirstName is printed on every letter
It sorts the data source by first name
It checks the spelling of each name
questions.why: A merge field is a placeholder: for each record, it is filled with that record's value from the data source, making a personalised copy.

long.q: Describe the steps needed to carry out a mail merge to send a personalised letter to 200 customers.
scheme: B1: create the master (standard) letter
B1: link it to the data source, e.g. a spreadsheet or database of customers
B1: insert merge fields (e.g. first name, address) in the right places
B1: preview, then merge to a new document, the printer or email

questions.q: A primary key
questions.why: No two records share it.

questions.q: Which field type suits a phone number?
questions.why: Leading zeros and '+' signs must be kept.

questions.q: Which field type should store a phone number such as 09876543210?
questions.why: Leading zeros would be lost in a number field, and no arithmetic is done on it.

questions.q: Which database validation check ensures that a student mark entered is between 0 and 100?
questions.why: A range check verifies that a numeric or date value falls between specified upper and lower allowable boundary values.

questions.q: Which query criteria find books published after 2015 that cost less than $20?
questions.why: Both conditions must be true, so AND is needed, and 'after' and 'less than' are strict, so > and < are used rather than >= and <=.

long.q: A library database stores details of its books. Design a table with four fields, give a suitable data type for each, and identify the primary key.
scheme: B1: a unique identifier field, e.g. BookID or ISBN (text/alphanumeric)
B1: it's the primary key because its value is different for every book
B1: Title: text
B1: e.g. DatePublished: date/time (or Price: currency)
B1: e.g. OnLoan: Boolean (Yes/No)

questions.q: A master slide is used to
o: set consistent design across all slides
questions.why: Change it once for every slide.

questions.q: What is a transition in a presentation?
o: Movement of an object on a slide
questions.why: An animation moves an object on a slide.

questions.q: What is a master slide used for?
o: Setting the same layout and style on every slide
questions.why: It keeps a presentation consistent.

questions.q: A presentation will run on a screen in a shop window with nobody there to control it. Which setting is needed?
o: Automatic slide timings with the show set to loop continuously
Advancing slides on each mouse click
questions.why: With timings and looping, the slides advance by themselves and restart at the end, so no presenter is needed.

questions.q: What are speaker notes in presentation software?
o: Large text shown on every slide
Printed handouts with three slides per page
Notes the presenter can see that are not shown to the audience on the slides
questions.why: Speaker notes are attached to each slide as prompts for the presenter and are not displayed on the projected slide.

long.q: Explain two benefits of using a master slide in a presentation, and give two items you would place on it.
scheme: B1: every slide has a consistent layout, font and colour scheme
B1: saves time: an item is placed once and changes update every slide
B1: an item, e.g. the company logo
B1: a second item, e.g. slide numbers, footer text, background

questions.q: Which formula adds cells A1 to A10?
questions.why: SUM with a range.

questions.q: $A$1 in a formula is
questions.why: It doesn't change when copied.

questions.q: =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail") returns 'Pass' when B2 is
questions.why: >= means greater than or equal to.

questions.q: What is the result of the spreadsheet formula =IF(B2>=50, "Pass", "Fail") when B2 contains 50?
questions.why: Because the comparison operator is >= (greater than or equal to), a value of 50 satisfies the condition and returns the true branch 'Pass'.

questions.q: Cell C2 contains =B2*$E$1. It is copied to C3. Which formula is in C3?
questions.why: The relative reference B2 becomes B3 when copied down one row, while the absolute reference $E$1 stays the same.

long.q: Cells B2:B31 hold the test marks of 30 students. Write formulas to: (a) find the average mark; (b) find the highest mark; (c) count how many students scored 50 or more; (d) in C2, show 'Pass' if B2 is 50 or more, otherwise 'Fail'.
scheme: B1: (a) =AVERAGE(B2:B31)
B1: (d) =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")

questions.q: In a web page, the presentation layer is created with
questions.why: HTML is content, CSS is presentation.

questions.q: A relative file path
o: is relative to the current page's folder
questions.why: Relative paths keep a site portable.

questions.q: Which part of a web page sets fonts and colours for every page?
questions.why: One stylesheet keeps the whole site consistent.

questions.q: What is a relative file path?
o: A full path from the drive's root
A path from the current file's location
questions.why: Relative paths keep links working when the site is moved.

questions.q: An external stylesheet makes all h1 headings blue, but one h1 on a page has an inline style making it red. What colour is that heading?
o: Purple, as the two styles are mixed
questions.why: In the cascade, an inline style takes priority over an external stylesheet, so that heading is red.

long.q: Write the HTML to: (a) make 'Our Team' a level 1 heading; (b) show the image team.jpg with the alternative text 'Our team'; (c) link the text 'Contact us' to contact.html; (d) attach the stylesheet style.css to the page.
scheme:
B1: (a)

Our Team
B1: (b)
B1: (c) Contact us
B1: (d) <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> inside the head section
